findings.claim: Tasks 4 and 5 sample only 599/600/700px and 999/1000/1100px, while the source check requires only nondecreasing minimum-width rules. A later valid minimum-width rule can therefore override a required layout after the sampled width and still earn 7/7. Independently, adding an ordered 800px rule that changes the cards to three columns passed 7/7 but Chromium measured three columns at 800, 999, 1000, and 1100px; adding an ordered 1200px rule that restores .page to block also passed 7/7 but Chromium measured a stacked page at 1200 and 1300px. Both contradict the README outcomes “from 600px” and “from 1000px” and its wide-desktop goal.

evidence.section: 4.1 Width: the width feature — width describes the viewport width for continuous media
2.1 Cascading Order, Order of Appearance — the last declaration in document order wins

findings.recommendation: Make the rendered checks cover every learner-authored wider minimum-width boundary that can affect .cards or .page, including an immediately-at/after-boundary probe, or reject later overrides of the assessed properties. Add public regressions for an ordered 800px three-column override and an ordered 1200px stacked-page override without disclosing completed declarations.

findings.claim: The reader deletes CSS comments before token recognition, joining tokens across a comment. Valid @media/**/screen rules therefore become @mediascreen in the checker. An independently completed route using comment-separated media and otherwise canonical conditions rendered the required one/two-column and stacked/grid transitions at every probed width in Chromium, but the public command reported 5 pass/2 fail (task 5 source lookup and media ordering). CSS tokenization consumes comments between successive token-consumption calls; it does not retokenize the already-emitted @media at-keyword together with the following screen identifier.

evidence.section: 4.3.1 Consume a token and 4.3.2 Consume comments — each token call consumes comments first, and consuming a comment returns nothing

findings.recommendation: When removing comments for this narrow reader, preserve a token boundary (for example, replace each comment with whitespace) rather than concatenating adjacent source fragments. Add a passing @media/**/screen regression and retain the failing @mediascreen regression.
